correctness.rationale: Same-type incidences never conflict; opposite types conflict exactly when they share just one of row or column. Hence a maximal set must take on either side every position compatible with all selected positions on the other. The resulting mutual closures are the two pure sets, b(b−1) identical transverse pairs, 4b oriented singleton/full-neighborhood pairs, and the complementary single-row blocks. In the last case each block has at least two positions; otherwise double closure adds an opposite-row position or fills the full pure side. If both rows are used and one has at least two positions, the other side is forced to a singleton or empty, so there are no additional cases. For b=1 the conflicts form a matching and for b=2 two disjoint K_{2,2}, giving the stated four counts in each small case. The binomial sum for the blocks, overlapping exponents and total follow; for b≥3 all mixed cases have size at most b+1, while each pure set has size 2b. The subdivisions have degeneracy at most two by deleting the subdivision vertices first. An independent run enumerated directly from third-edge witnesses for each b=1,…,5, matching the full distributions, including the collisions at b=3 and b=4.
residual_risks: The replay is finite; the mutual-closure argument supplies exhaustion for arbitrary b.

evidence: In the prior formula 2|M|+mc(G−V(M)), for K_{2,b} the values by matching size 0,1,2 are 2b,b+1,4; only the empty matching attains 2b for b≥3. The two ordered full cuts of the connected bipartite base then give the maximum census.

The all-set polynomial counts partial incidence choices as well as saturated ones. For the mixed cuts with no double incidences, even saturating a fixed cut need not be globally maximal: a one-edge star allows doubling that incidence.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The maximum statements are covered. The maximal tiers require additional extension constraints: for a nonpure mixed saturated cut with one center row, both opposite stars must contain at least two edges. Such constraints and the exact binomial contributions are beyond numerical specialization of the all-packing polynomial.

originality.rationale: The prior general S(G) decomposition of all packings and maximum-cut formula materially cover the feasible packings and imply the maximum size and its two attaining sets here for b≥3. The supported distinct part is the explicit classification and cardinality distribution of all inclusion-maximal sets, including the gap, not that prior decomposition or its extremal consequences. This requires analyzing extensions that can change the matching or center sets; the inspected prior result does not give a maximality filter or the mixed-type contributions.
residual_risks: An equivalent maximal-biclique or maximal-independent-set account could be unindexed.

value.rationale: The polynomial enumerates the possible sizes of saturated packings, not just which packings can attain the maximum. The four-type description explains how exponentially many smaller maximal choices coexist with only two largest ones. Unbounded missing sizes on connected bipartite graphs of degeneracy two provide a natural structural contrast with the familiar scalar extremum.
residual_risks: No comparable distribution is claimed for general theta graphs or arbitrary subdivisions.
